nodes.name: Carbon cloth pretreatment
nodes.procedure: A 1 × 1 cm² CC was used as the substrate for the synthesis of HEA materials. Briefly, the CC was ultrasonicated in acetone solution for 5 min, then rinsed several times with deionized (DI) water, and dried in an oven at 60°C for 1 h. After drying, the CC was immersed in a mixed solution of concentrated sulfuric acid and nitric acid with a volume ratio of 3:1 at room temperature for 12 h. After soaking, the CC was washed several times with DI water to remove the remaining acids. Finally, it was put into a 60°C oven to dry and set aside for further use.

nodes.name: FeCoNiLaPd electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The synthesis of FeCoNiLaPd was carried out via a facile electrodeposition strategy. Briefly, FeCl₂ (6.38 mg), CoCl₂ (6.49 mg), NiCl₂ (6.48 mg), LaCl₃ (12.26 mg), PdCl₂ (8.87 mg), and (C₂H₅)₄N(PF₆) (5.50 mg) were mixed and added to the organic solution consisting of CH₃CN (60 mL), CH₃CH₂OH (20 mL), and HCON(CH₃)₂ (20 mL). After the mixture was sufficiently stirred, electrodeposition experiments were conducted. During the process, CC, a titanium mesh, and Hg/HgO electrodes were used as the working, counter, and reference electrodes, respectively. The electrodeposition reaction was performed in a constant voltage of 3.0 V for 30 min under stable stirring at room temperature. After the deposition processes, the working electrode was washed several times with ethanol and DI water to obtain the final FeCoNiLaPd HEA catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: Distinct alloy phase peaks at 40.1°, 46.1°, and 68.2° attributed to (111), (200), and (220) facets of FeCoNiLaPd with absence of individual metal patterns.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1b presents the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of the FeCoNiLaPd material with distinct alloy phase peaks at 40.1, 46.1, and 68.2° attributed to the (111), (200), and (220) facets, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic percentages in FeCoNiLaPd are Fe 18.8%, Co 22.6%, Ni 19.2%, La 31.2%, Pd 8.2%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The quantitative analysis of inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) shows that the atomic percentages of Fe, Co, Ni, La, and Pd metals in FeCoNiLaPd are 18.8, 22.6, 19.2, 31.2, and 8.2%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: FESEM reveals numerous ordered microsized spherical aggregations densely distributed on CC fibers for FeCoNiLaPd.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphological characteristics of the sample were examined by field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), as illustrated in Figure 1d and Figure S3, which reveals the presence of numerous ordered microsized spherical aggregations.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS reveals multiple valence states in FeCoNiLaPd: Co (Co⁰ at 777.1/792.3 eV, Co²⁺ at 782.6/797.9 eV, Co³⁺ at 780.7/796.8 eV), Fe (Fe⁰ at 706.4 eV, Fe²⁺ at 710.4 eV, Fe³⁺ at 712.4 eV), higher Fe²⁺ and Ni⁰ proportions vs FeCoNiPd, Pd²⁺ shift to lower binding energies, La³⁺ present.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in Figure 2a, the XPS Co 2p spectra reveal the presence of three distinct valence states, Co⁰ Co²⁺ and Co³⁺... the XPS La 3d spectrum of FeCoNiLaPd shows a considerable amount of the oxidized La species (La³⁺).

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoNiLaPd HEA shows considerable specific surface area and unique mesoporous feature with larger surface area and smaller average pore size compared to FeCoNiPd.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HEA materials show a considerable specific surface area and a unique mesoporous feature (Figure S1 and Table S1). Compared with FeCoNiPd, FeCoNiLaPd HEA has a larger specific surface area and smaller average pore size.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during OER shows increasing intensities of peaks at 450 and 525 cm⁻¹ ascribed to e_g and A_{1g} vibrations of Ni(FeCo)OOH species, indicating surface reconstruction to metal hydroxyl oxides.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 6a, the intensities of Raman peaks at 450 and 525 cm⁻¹ respectively ascribed to the e_g-bonding vibration and A_{1g} stretching vibrational bonding of Ni(FeCo)OOH species increase with the applied potential.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ DRIFTS during OER shows peaks at 3250, 1650, and 1210 cm⁻¹ for *OH, H-O-H stretching, and *OOH bending vibrations, confirming metal hydroxyl oxide formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, in situ DRIFTS peaks with voltage increasing from 1.25 to 2.15 V are visibly observed at 3250, 1650, and 1210 cm⁻¹ ascribed to the stretching vibration of *OH and H-O-H species and the bending vibration of *OOH, respectively.
